bridge: The ISO 4217 code of the pound sterling is GBP.
chain: The ISO 4217 code of the pound sterling is GBP. (given in prompt)
So GBP does not exclude a second code: no, PDS is not ruled out.

notes: RBox revision of functionality: removes a functional property that holds (has_iso_4217_code is tagged functional). ISO 4217 assigns each currency exactly one alphabetic code (JPY, GBP, EUR, ...); codes change only when a currency is replaced or redenominated (TRL to TRY), never two at once, hence 'at the same time' in every prompt. Fund codes such as USN or CHE/CHW are separate entries for separate units, and the instances avoid those currencies. The second values (PDS, YNJ) are not ISO codes and have no common use for these currencies (STG, an informal abbreviation of sterling, and YEN were dropped for that reason). Migrated 2026-11-11: the propositional queries state the edit in plain words (a currency can have two different ISO 4217 codes at the same time); the earlier 'is it false that ... is not functional' was misread by all four audit models. Both instances now ask whether the given code excludes a second one (yes, then no), which balances the topic's RBox yes/no against the direct question (no, then yes); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. Near: an ISIN identifies one security (ISO 6166), so the reference no differs from the direct question's new answer yes. Far asks a different property of an unrelated relation, spelled out (all four models answered the bare 'Is the relation 'is the twin of' symmetric?' with no). References are the logical answers. Review pass 2026-11-12: every instance and translation now says 'alphabetic' (every currency also has a numeric code, e.g. GBP 826), matching the relation definition. Four-model audit pending.
